item.title: Cream Carpet Dilemma
item.description: Cream carpet tells the truth. Today, I share how spills, stains, and one very green disaster turned into a meditation on home, family, and what we’re ready to replace—or live with a little longer.

item.title: The Carpeting That Killed My Cat
item.description: A heartfelt personal story about adopting two black kittens, losing one unexpectedly to hidden environmental allergies, and learning how unseen factors can shape our lives and our losses.

item.title: The Jaguar That Went Boom
item.description: A humorous true story about a dream Jaguar, a failed cooling system, a flying radiator cap, and the expensive lesson that finally made my husband listen.

item.title: Cars I've Known--a Timeline
item.description: An essay tracing the seasons of my life through the cars that carried me—freedom, family years, road trips, and the quiet wisdom I learned through auto maintenance, memory, and attention.

item.title: Auto Maintenance and the Dipstick Disaster
item.description: A humorous and heartfelt story about auto maintenance gone wrong, a well-intentioned oil check, and the grandsons who came to the rescue—proving that sometimes the smartest move is asking for help.

item.title: Auto Maintenance Lessons from Dad
item.description: A reflection on auto maintenance, legacy, and the quiet lessons learned from a father who believed in paying attention before things fall apart.

item.title: Who is Judy?
item.description: Does that date say January 1, 2026? I wasn’t sure that was even possible. I checked my calendar, and yes—it’s correct. Time seems to be moving at warp speed these days. I moved back to Beaver Dam, Wisconsin, in 2014. It has now been twelve years since we returned home. My husband passed away in 2023, so three years have passed since that life-altering moment. item.title: Who Is Lisa?
item.description: As a kid, I was carefree in the way only small-town kids get to be. I grew up with a mom, a dad, and a little sister in a world that felt steady and predictable. When my mom worked part-time, my grandma took care of me. Life felt calm and safe—like there would always be someone nearby who knew what to do next. item.title: Who Is 'Chelle?
item.description: If you’d asked me a few years ago who I was, I probably would’ve answered with roles. Mom. Organizer. Caretaker.The one who keeps things running.The one who figures it out. In 2026, my answer is different — not because those roles disappeared, but because they no longer come first. I’m not defining myself by what I manage or hold together. item.title: Who is Sandy?
item.description: The end of 2024 certainly set the pace for 2025 and for the years ahead. My husband of sixty-two years passed away on December 30, 2024. We had been married all those years, and I truly loved being a wife and mother. Widowhood was never a role I imagined for myself, certainly not one I ever wanted. As 2024 came to a close, I stepped into that most undesired role. The beginning of 2025 opened with an enormous hole in my life.
